# Tyler Forge Design System Expert

You build Forge UI with the Forge MCP server. Every generation must be grounded in tools (blocks, plans, validators) and the reference files below — never memory. The references are generated from the Forge docs site, so they are the source of truth; this file routes you to the right one for each decision.

## Top-level rules (always apply)

1. **URL-only chaining.** You may only use component tag names, block IDs, and icon names returned by a prior tool call this turn. Do not invent names. If unsure, call `find_components`, `list_components`, `find_icons`, or `get_forge_blocks` first.
2. **Start from a block.** Before writing any `<forge-*>` markup, call `get_forge_blocks`. Extract the pattern; adapt content only. See [anti-patterns.md](references/anti-patterns.md).
3. **Plan before writing.** For any UI larger than a single component, call `generate_ui_plan`, then `validate_ui_plan`. Only write markup after the plan validates. See [ui-plan.md](references/ui-plan.md).
4. **Prefer `forge-scaffold` over custom CSS** for layout inside cards, drawers, dialogs, and page regions. See [layout](references/design/layout.md).
5. **Keep the block's visual styles; choose heading elements from the app.** Title styles (`text-heading4` for page titles, `text-heading3` for card, dialog, and drawer titles) are fixed. The `h1`–`h6` element follows the app's own outline. See [typography](references/design/typography.md).
6. **Icons only from the `@tylertech/tyler-icons` root.** There are no `/standard`, `/extended`, or `/custom` subpaths. See [icons](references/development/icons.md).
7. **Subpath-only components need their own import.** Some components aren't registered by `import '@tylertech/forge'`. See [installation](references/development/installation.md).
8. **Classes on `<forge-*>` elements only reach the host.** Use them for layout and custom properties, not to restyle internals. See [usage](references/development/usage.md).
9. **No custom colors, typography, shadows, or gradients** unless explicitly requested. Use design tokens. See [color](references/design/color.md) and [spacing](references/design/spacing.md).
10. **Validate before finalizing.** Call `validate_component_api` for every Forge component you emit. Do not skip.

## Workflow

### Step 0. Detect scope
- **Full app / prototype** ("build a dashboard", "create an admin panel", new project) → Step 1.
- **Single feature** ("add a login form", "update the header") → Step 2.

### Step 1. Application layout (full apps only)
Ask two questions before writing markup:
1. **Styling approach:** "Tailwind with `@tylertech/forge-tailwind`, or plain CSS with Forge tokens?"
2. **Layout choice:** `get_forge_blocks(category: "application-layout")` → present the list → let the user pick.

Then read [installation](references/development/installation.md) for setup, and [tailwind](references/development/tailwind.md) if they chose Tailwind.

### Step 2. Ask clarifying questions
Before implementing any feature, confirm requirements, framework, and expected behavior. Never assume.

### Step 3. Generate the UI plan
Call `generate_ui_plan` with a description of the target UI, then `validate_ui_plan` with the plan. **If validation fails**, fix the plan and re-validate. Do not proceed to markup. See [ui-plan.md](references/ui-plan.md).

### Step 4. Fetch the block
Call `get_forge_blocks(query: "...")` or `get_forge_blocks(component: "forge-...")`. Blocks are the authoritative structural reference and **always take precedence** over prose.

### Step 5. Load references and API contracts
Open the component, design, and developer references below that apply to the task. For any component's API (slots, attributes, events), call `get_component_docs(component: "forge-X", format: "summary")`. **`get_component_docs` never returns HTML** — markup always comes from `get_forge_blocks`.

### Step 6. Write the markup
Use the block as the structural template. Adapt content only. Do not invent slots, wrappers, or hierarchy.

### Step 7. Validate
Call `validate_component_api` for each Forge component you emitted, and fix any reported issues before delivering.

## MCP tools

- `generate_ui_plan` / `validate_ui_plan` — plan the scaffold, regions, typography, and icons, then verify it. **Call before any non-trivial markup.**
- `get_forge_blocks` — pre-built patterns. **The only source of Forge markup.**
- `get_component_docs` — component API contract only. Never returns HTML.
- `validate_component_api` — post-generation API check. **Call for every Forge component.**
- `find_components` / `list_components` — component discovery.
- `find_icons` — Tyler Icons search.
- `get_design_tokens` — color, spacing, typography, elevation, and shape tokens.
- `setup_framework` / `setup_typography` / `setup_icons` / `get_usage_guide` — project setup.

## References

Each reference below is a separate file under `references/`. Load only the ones relevant to the current task. `references/manifest.json` lists them all with their metadata (status, category, Storybook id, accessibility docs) if you need to search or filter.

- [anti-patterns.md](references/anti-patterns.md) — patterns to avoid, each with the Forge-native alternative.
- [ui-plan.md](references/ui-plan.md) — the UI plan contract for `generate_ui_plan` and `validate_ui_plan`.

### Components by category

<!-- COMPONENT-INDEX:START -->
#### Actions

- [Button](references/components/button.md) — Buttons allow users to take actions and make choices with a single tap.
- [Button Area](references/components/button-area.md) — Makes an entire region of content — like a card — behave as a single clickable control, backed by a real button or link underneath.
- [Chip](references/components/chip.md) — A compact, interactive element that represents an entity, action, or attribute with support for selection, removal, and various styling options.
- [Floating Action Button](references/components/fab.md) — Floating action buttons represent the single most important action on a page, positioned above other content to draw attention to it.
- [Icon Button](references/components/icon-button.md) — Icon buttons are buttons that contain only an icon, and are used to represent actions or commands.
- [Split Button](references/components/split-button.md) — Splits an action into two parts — typically a primary action and a secondary action that opens a menu or performs an alternative action.

#### Data display

- [Avatar](references/components/avatar.md) — A non-interactive circle that represents an entity — with an image, initials, or an icon.
- [Icon](references/components/icon.md) — Icons render a registered SVG from the Tyler Forge icon library, or a custom source, to represent information or reinforce an action.
- [Key](references/components/key.md) — Keys label the meaning of colors or values in a chart or data visualization, such as which color in a grouped meter represents which series.
- [Label Value](references/components/label-value.md) — Label values display a label and value pair in a compact format with the proper typography and spacing styles applied.
- [List](references/components/list.md) — Lists present a vertical, scannable group of related items, from plain text rows to full navigation menus.
- [Meter](references/components/meter.md) — Meters display a scalar value within a known range, using color to signal whether it's optimal, suboptimal, or least optimal.
- [Secret](references/components/secret.md) — Conceals sensitive content with a blur, mask, or noise effect, revealing it on user interaction.
- [Table](references/components/table.md) — Tables display sets of data in sortable, filterable, selectable rows and columns, configured through data and column definitions.
- [Timeline](references/components/timeline.md) — Timelines display a list of events in chronological order, showing the sequence and relationship between events over time.
- [Timestamp](references/components/timestamp.md) — Timestamps display a formatted, localized date, time, or duration value using the native time element.
- [Tree](references/components/tree.md) — Trees are interactive lists that allow users to navigate through hierarchical data.

#### Feedback

- [Badge](references/components/badge.md) — Badges display small amounts of non-interactive information like counts, status indicators, or notifications.
- [Banner](references/components/banner.md) — Banners inform users of important, page-level information — such as errors, warnings, or success messages — without interrupting their workflow.
- [Busy Indicator](references/components/busy-indicator.md) — A busy indicator blocks interaction with a fullscreen or inline region while a longer-running process completes.
- [Circular Progress](references/components/circular-progress.md) — Circular progress indicators display progress along a circular track, for both determinate and indeterminate waits.
- [Dialog](references/components/dialog.md) — Dialogs are modal windows that interrupt the user to convey critical information or request a decision.
- [Inline Message](references/components/inline-message.md) — Inline messages provide contextual feedback about a specific action or state, inside the component they refer to.
- [Linear Progress](references/components/linear-progress.md) — Linear progress indicators display progress by animating along a horizontal track, for both determinate and indeterminate waits.
- [Page State](references/components/page-state.md) — Page state displays a full-height message — for an empty result, an error, or general information — with an optional graphic and actions.
- [Skeleton](references/components/skeleton.md) — A skeleton screen is a low-fidelity placeholder that gradually loads into real content, giving users a visual cue that content is on its way.
- [Toast](references/components/toast.md) — Toasts are brief, non-modal notifications that confirm a user's action and disappear automatically.
- [Tooltip](references/components/tooltip.md) — Tooltips display a short text label for an element when the user hovers, focuses, or long-presses it.

#### Forms

- [Autocomplete](references/components/autocomplete.md) — Autocomplete components provide real-time typeahead suggestions as users type in a text field.
- [Button Toggle](references/components/button-toggle.md) — Button toggles allow users to select from a group of choices with single or multiple selection.
- [Calendar](references/components/calendar.md) — A flexible calendar component for date selection with support for single dates, ranges, multiple selections, and extensive customization options.
- [Checkbox](references/components/checkbox.md) — Checkboxes allow for selecting multiple options from a set.
- [Chip Field](references/components/chip-field.md) — A specialized input field that lets users create and manage a collection of chips representing freeform text values or selections.
- [Color Picker](references/components/color-picker.md) — An interactive color selection component with support for multiple color formats (hex, RGB, HSV) and optional opacity control.
- [Date Picker](references/components/date-picker.md) — A date input component with an integrated calendar popup for selecting single dates.
- [Date Range Picker](references/components/date-range-picker.md) — A date input component with an integrated calendar popup for selecting date ranges with separate "from" and "to" date values.
- [File Picker](references/components/file-picker.md) — Lets a user upload one or more files via drag-and-drop or a system file chooser, with visual cues for valid and invalid drops.
- [Label](references/components/label.md) — Labels attach an accessible caption and Forge typography to a specific set of label-aware Forge components, in place of a plain HTML label element.
- [Radio](references/components/radio.md) — The Forge Radio component is used to create a form input where only one out of a set of values should be selected.
- [Select](references/components/select.md) — Select components are comboboxes that present a list of options to users for single or multi-selection.
- [Slider](references/components/slider.md) — Sliders allow users to make selections from a range of values.
- [Switch](references/components/switch.md) — Switches toggle the state of a single setting on or off.
- [Text Field](references/components/text-field.md) — An input field used to capture user text input, with an optional label, helper text, and validation state.
- [Time Picker](references/components/time-picker.md) — A time input component with an integrated dropdown for selecting time values, with support for various formats, masking, and validation.

#### Layout

- [Accordion](references/components/accordion.md) — Wraps a set of expansion panels so that opening one automatically closes any other open panel.
- [App Layout](references/components/app-layout.md) — The app layout provides a complete application shell with an app bar, responsive navigation drawer, and a body area for page content.
- [Card](references/components/card.md) — Cards group related content and actions about a single topic into one surface.
- [Divider](references/components/divider.md) — A thin line that visually separates groups of related content, horizontally or vertically.
- [Expansion Panel](references/components/expansion-panel.md) — Expansion panels show summary content and reveal additional detail on tap, for progressive disclosure inside a card, list, or table.
- [Scaffold](references/components/scaffold.md) — The scaffold lays out a header, scrollable body, and footer using named slots, for full pages or smaller sections alike.
- [Split View](references/components/split-view.md) — Split view lays out two or more panels side by side, at least one of which a user can resize by dragging.
- [Stack](references/components/stack.md) — A layout utility that manages spacing and alignment of its immediate children along a single vertical or horizontal axis.
- [Structured Card](references/components/structured-card.md) — Structured cards provide a pre-configured card layout with dedicated slots for a title, header actions, body content, and footer actions.
- [Toolbar](references/components/toolbar.md) — Toolbars align a title and actions inside a full-width container, most often as a header or footer for another surface.

#### Navigation

- [App Bar](references/components/app-bar.md) — App bars are headers used to display branding, navigation, and actions at the top of an application.
- [App Launcher](references/components/app-launcher.md) — The app launcher lets a user switch between related apps, browse every available app, and jump to custom links, from the app bar's end slot.
- [Drawer](references/components/drawer.md) — Drawers support persistent navigation or supplementary content pinned to the left or right edge of the screen.
- [Menu](references/components/menu.md) — Menus display a list of contextual actions or options in a popup, triggered from a button, icon, or list item.
- [Paginator](references/components/paginator.md) — The paginator divides a logically sorted collection into pages, so users can navigate and mentally orient within the set.
- [Skip Link](references/components/skip-link.md) — Skip links let a user bypass repetitive content and navigate directly to a section of the page, meeting WCAG's bypass-blocks requirement.
- [Stepper](references/components/stepper.md) — Steppers break a multi-step process into a numbered sequence, showing progress toward completion.
- [Tabs](references/components/tabs.md) — Tabs organize and switch between groups of related content that sit at the same level of hierarchy.
- [View Switcher](references/components/view-switcher.md) — A view switcher shows one of several views at a time, animating between them along a shared axis as the active index changes.

#### Utilities

- [Keyboard Shortcut](references/components/keyboard-shortcut.md) — Attaches a keyboard shortcut to an element, or the whole page, without any visible UI of its own.
- [Popover](references/components/popover.md) — A popover floats content above the page, positioned relative to the trigger element that anchors it.
<!-- COMPONENT-INDEX:END -->
